planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in a site protected from the hottest afternoon sun.

directions: Selected for its heart-shaped foliage that emerges apricot-orange, matures through gold and chartreuse tones, and finishes green by late summer, giving a continually shifting multicolor canopy across the growing season. Lavender-pink pea-like flowers appear on bare branches in early spring ahead of the foliage display. It grows into a small, broadly rounded tree well suited as a specimen or understory accent. Light afternoon shade helps prevent leaf scorch in hot summer climates, while full morning sun intensifies the new foliage color.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring; vigorous growth fills out quickly once established.

directions: Developed by North Carolina State University breeders, this redbud is known for heart-shaped foliage that shifts through an unusually wide color range each season, with new growth emerging orange-red, aging through yellow and apricot tones, and settling into green with purple-tinged edges by summer. Lavender-pink pea-like flowers appear on bare branches in early spring before leaf-out. It grows noticeably more vigorously and uniformly upright than many other colored-foliage redbud selections. Light shade in the afternoon helps preserve the most vivid foliage colors through the heat of summer.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Give this vigorous hybrid ample room to reach its full spread; plant in fall or early spring.

directions: A vigorous hybrid dogwood bred at Rutgers University, producing some of the largest flower bracts of any dogwood, often six inches or more across, in creamy white atop the foliage in late spring to early summer. Growth is notably fast and the tree develops a strong, well-branched habit reaching tree size more quickly than most kousa selections. It combines good resistance to anthracnose, powdery mildew, and dogwood borer, problems that limit many flowering dogwood plantings. Grow as an understory or specimen tree in light shade with moist, well-drained, acidic soil.
sources: Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station
